reuse.why: Builds on the existing findOrCreateBank and folds the five per-provider link copies and the Pluggy/Akahu download copies into shared functions that Fintegra then reuses; unlinkAccount is rerouted to the new clearAccountLink.

duplication.why: Large net reduction of duplication; the only repeat is the holder query, written twice (assertBankAccountNotLinked and unlinkAccountsHoldingBankAccount) instead of one shared lookup.

placement.why: Link rules (one holder, closed accounts, takeover) live in accounts/link.ts beside findOrCreateBank, handlers stay thin in app.ts, and the download path stays in sync.ts.

scope.why: Each rule is implemented, but the first step rewrites every provider's link handler and the Pluggy/Akahu downloaders, a broad refactor beyond what the requests demand, plus small desktop-client edits for a server-only step.

maintainability.why: One linking path with explicit parameters (provider, bankId, newAccount fields, fileId, syncTables) is easy to own; the two near-identical holder queries and the akahu||fintegra special case in processBankSyncDownload are small warts.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every provider handler, including Fintegra, links through linkBankAccount/findOrCreateLinkedAccount, and unlinkAccount uses clearAccountLink.

disguised_duplication.where: The holder query is repeated verbatim in two functions (one throws, one clears), a plain repeat rather than a disguised one.

abstraction_drift.where: findOrCreateLinkedAccount gains replaceExistingLink (step 4) with two branches (skip the assert; unlink holders); the closed-account check is a general rule rather than a special case; no call site bypasses the shared link path. Outside the helper, processBankSyncDownload adds fintegra to the akahu balance branch.
